title: Evil Dead Burn
review: Weird how they're having birthday party with a cake and presents, at tiny table in a club next to the dance floor and stairs. There's strobes flashing in their face and it's somehow quiet enough to talk. It's a jumble of attempts to make the viewer uncomfortable show gross kills, and there's not much of a cohesive through line between these scenes. Some just seem like contrivances, working backwards from an idea for a punchy camera angle or gross-out stunt. For example, at the start, I think that the only reason they're in a club is so that there can be the visual gag of smash cutting to a twerking ass. (It's referred to as a restaurant later.) The only reason for the cremation scene was so they could show the worker dancing from a camera inside the furnace. The only reason they're all in a derelict house together is so that people can smash through walls in the event of a zombie curse. The CGI was fine, until the final boss who looked like shit. It's increasingly bizarre to me that they have rebooted this series without any of the comedy. The grandmother has some lame jokes, but it's very different to the humour from the originals, and far worse. The drama did nothing for me, so the first half especially was a real slog, before things got really evil. It's also too long, and I'm not just saying that because it's bad. Horror movies have to have engaging and worthwhile stories to justify being longer than 90 minutes. Think {Midsommar} or {The Silence of the Lambs}. If it's just going to be a slasher with a basic plot, does it really need to as long as those?
spoilers: I enjoy the trope of people scrabbling desperately for a weapon in a kitchen, and only finding something silly. Here it's the electric carving knife. {Weapons} has a good one. So did the previous {Evil Dead Rise}.
